payload.title: fgos-coding-exploring's lock-decisions-and-write-context.md example omits --id, causing unscoped…
payload.description:
fgos-coding-exploring's lock-decisions-and-write-context.md example omits --id, causing unscoped fgos decision writes.

fgos-coding-exploring/references/lock-decisions-and-write-context.md's own Step 2 example command for `fgos decision` omits `--id "<item-id>"` entirely (`fgos decision --text "<D-ID>: ..." --rationale "..." --relation none`), unlike sibling reference docs in the same skill family (gate-mechanics.md and gate-auto-approve-mechanics.md's own auto-approve decision lines, which both correctly include `--id "<item-id>"`). A session following lock-decisions-and-write-context.md's example literally logs an unscoped (repo-wide, not item-attached) decision instead of one attached to the item -- only caught later via a context-render "no state.decisions record exists yet for <id>" refusal or a row-count mismatch.

Live-hit 2026-08-24 during tsk-5et's own exploring pass: two fgos decision calls followed this doc's example verbatim (no --id, no positional id either), both landed unscoped, had to be re-logged with --id added.

Related to tsk-5op ("fgos decision CLI silently drops a positional item-id instead of erroring") but distinct and NOT closed by it: tsk-5op's own fix directions (positional[0] ?? flags.id fallback, or generic unexpected-positional-argument validation) only address a caller who passes the id positionally -- they do nothing for a caller who follows this doc's own example exactly (no positional argument at all, --id simply never in the command).

Fix: add --id "<item-id>" to lock-decisions-and-write-context.md's own example command, and audit the other fgos-coding-* skill reference docs for the same omission before assuming this is the only instance.

Resubmission note: an earlier submission of this exact item (tsk-4dc, 2026-08-24 ~23:08-23:19) was fully carried through discovery/planning/validating with real research/plan/gate-approval, then its own .fgos state record vanished entirely from the store around 23:32:06 with no trace in any event shard -- a live-hit of the still-open tsk-24e/tsk-1ji data-loss mechanism. The git-committed work (plan.md/RESEARCH.md) survived on the now-orphaned branch fgw/tsk-4dc and is being ported forward into this new item's own docs.
